clue.text: One who transmits from a Scottish island to S.E.13 ?

parts.note: Lewis is the northern part of the largest island of the Outer Hebrides
a radio ham is an amateur who transmits on the airwaves

explanation.surface: A radio amateur on a Hebridean island is sending a message down to a London postal district.
explanation.walkthrough: S.E.13 is the London postcode of the borough of LEWISHAM, in south-east London; 'from' and 'to' are link words here.
explanation.definitionFit: The London postal district SE13 covers this south-east London borough, so the postcode names the place.

clue.text: Surgeon as roll-maker ?

definitions.meaning: Joseph ..., the British surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery
one who draws up a roll or list of names

explanation.definitionFit: The antiseptic pioneer bears the name, and read literally the word is someone compiling lists.

clue.text: Animal doctor has one in two perhaps

indicators.note: in places the doctor and the one inside the rearranged word
perhaps hints that the word two may appear in another form

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
a means one

explanation.surface: A vet has a patient that might be one of a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns TWO into WOT, which holds MB and A.
explanation.definitionFit: This burrowing marsupial of Australia is an animal.

clue.text: An example on board of " December when they wed ' ?

definitions.meaning: a chess position in which the player to move has no legal move, a drawn game
a spouse grown old, as in a December-and-May marriage of an old man to a young woman

explanation.definitionFit: The chess draw is a position on the board, and split it describes an old, worn-out partner.

clue.text: Fast time, but a sorry start

definitions.meaning: the first day of Lent, a season of fasting
the start of a season of penitence, marked with ashes as a sign of sorrow

explanation.definitionFit: Lent, the Christian fasting season, begins on this day, when penitents receive ashes as a sign of repentance.

clue.text: Mark of battle Jack brought home from Egypt ?

parts.note: a wound from fighting leaves a scar
a jack tar is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the crossword abbreviation for one

explanation.surface: A sailor returns from Egyptian service bearing a war wound.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred beetle carved as an amulet is a classic souvenir of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: He heard the nightingale with the emperor

definitions.text: He heard the nightingale with the emperor

parts.words: He heard the nightingale with the emperor
parts.note: Keats's Ode to a Nightingale: the song 'was heard in ancient days by emperor and' a lowly figure, the court fool

explanation.surface: A courtier listened to birdsong in the imperial garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats wrote that the nightingale's voice 'was heard / In ancient days by emperor and clown'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats pairs the emperor with a clown, a rustic or jester, as the humblest hearer of the bird.

clue.text: Cancels a hundred in dress design

indicators.note: design means the letters are worked into a new pattern

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A dressmaker scraps a hundred of her dress patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: To revoke or annul an order or law is to cancel it.

clue.text: Bairnsfather and Dornford Yates characters sound a fruity pair

definitions.note: the clue's adjective describes the noun answer, a kind of fruit

indicators.note: sound says the two names together are heard as a word

parts.note: Bruce Bairnsfather's famous cartoon soldier was Old Bill; Dornford Yates wrote the Berry and Co. stories, about Berry and his family

explanation.surface: Two characters from popular fiction whose names together sound like produce.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Bill and Berry are two characters of early 20th-century British popular fiction; said together they give the name of a small blue berry.
explanation.definitionFit: The bilberry is a small dark-blue fruit of moorland shrubs, related to the blueberry.

clue.text: Playful companion for tea

parts.note: the word that keeps tea company in the title of a stage play, 'Tea and ...', Robert Anderson's 1953 drama

explanation.surface: A jolly friend to share a pot of tea with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playful' means 'in a play': the play is 'Tea and Sympathy', and the word paired with tea in its title is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the play title the word partners tea, and the phrase 'tea and sympathy' means kindly comfort.

clue.text: Ancient relic-two shillings in wrapper

indicators.note: the two shillings are placed inside the wrapper, as the word in says

parts.note: foil is a metal sheet used for wrapping food
S stands for a shilling in old British money, so two shillings give two Ss

explanation.surface: An old curio wrapped up together with a couple of pre-decimal coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a British coin before 1971, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: A preserved remain of an organism from a past geological age is a relic of very ancient times.

clue.text: Kings who secretly post agents out of the East

parts.note: to plant someone is to place them secretly, as a spy

indicators.note: out of here means outside of, so the agents go round the East

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Monarchs who covertly send spies away from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' looks like 'leaving', but it means the agents stand outside E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenet dynasty supplied the kings of England from Henry II to Richard III.

clue.text: Escape the previous day without publicity

indicators.note: the old sense of without as outside, so the previous day goes round the publicity

parts.note: the eve is the day before an event
an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: Someone slipped away the day before, avoiding the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking' but here means 'outside', as in old hymns.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge or elude something is to get away from it.

clue.text: With musk-roses, unusually elegant in appearance

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Something looking strangely elegant alongside a bed of musk-roses.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes A Midsummer Night's Dream: 'With sweet musk-roses and with eglantine'; 'appearance' just rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line pairs musk-roses with this sweetbriar, so the quotation fragment points to the companion plant.

clue.text: Banger diet for 600 ?

parts.note: a cannon is something that goes bang
fodder is food, the diet given to livestock

explanation.surface: Sausages as the menu for a big crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' suggests a British sausage but is the gun; the 600 are Tennyson's Light Brigade, 'Into the valley of Death rode the six hundred'.
explanation.definitionFit: The doomed Light Brigade were soldiers sent to die needlessly, the classic case of expendable troops.

clue.text: Omission of the bird's-eye view ?

definitions.meaning: a failure to notice or include something
a view looking down from over the top, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: A slip or failure to notice is a lapse, and split in two it gives a view from above.

clue.text: A mark for the sucker

definitions.meaning: the centre of a target, the mark aimed at
a large round peppermint sweet sucked slowly, a British boiled sweet

explanation.definitionFit: The target's centre is what archers aim at, and the striped boiled sweet of that name is sucked.

clue.text: Anxiety-caused, by noise ?

definitions.meaning: the loss of quiet, read as dis- plus a word for silence

explanation.definitionFit: Worry and unease are inner unrest, and split up the word reads as quiet undone, which noise brings.

clue.text: Fifty star power

parts.note: a world power whose flag carries fifty stars, one for each of its member states

explanation.surface: A celebrity of the highest rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The American flag shows fifty stars, one per state, and the country is a great power.

clue.text: Than Snow White, none of course

definitions.text: Than Snow White, none of course

parts.words: Than Snow White, none of course
parts.note: the magic mirror's verdict that nobody is more beautiful than Snow White

explanation.surface: Naturally nobody outshines Snow White.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fairy tale the mirror says Snow White is fairest of all, so of course none is more beautiful than her.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of the word for beautiful completes the familiar fairy-tale judgment.

clue.text: Cannot Richard qualify for this poetic status ?

definitions.text: Cannot Richard qualify for this poetic status ?

parts.words: Cannot Richard qualify for this poetic status ?
parts.note: read 'cannot' as a verb meaning shut out and Richard by his short form; the two words said together give the adjective for a poet

explanation.surface: Is a man called Richard barred from being a poet laureate?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cannot' is a word meaning exclude, and Richard's nickname follows; spoken together they sound like the adjective for a bard.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, and the adjective describes the standing of such a poet.

clue.text: Wind up out of time holding twenty bob

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: late means past the proper time
twenty shillings (bob) made one pound, a quid, so twenty bob is I (one) QUID

explanation.surface: A tardy person clutching a pound note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bob' is British slang for a shilling, and a 'quid' is a pound, which was worth twenty shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: To close down a company and sell off its assets is to bring its affairs to an end.

clue.text: Portrait of a P.R.O. ?

definitions.meaning: a likeness or picture of someone
the public impression that a public relations officer works to shape

explanation.definitionFit: A likeness is a picture, and a publicist's job is a client's public reputation.

clue.text: Theatre shows one of the 18 in South Africa

indicators.note: the state goes inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: 18-across is the fifty-state union, and Cal is an abbreviation of one state, California

explanation.surface: A playhouse staging a show from somewhere in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: La Scala in Milan is the world-famous opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan's famous opera house is generally called by this short name.

clue.text: The Spanish pilgrim to Mecca returns to the prophet

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: returns says the pilgrim's word is turned round to go back

parts.note: a haji is a Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca

explanation.surface: A Spanish pilgrim comes back from Mecca to his prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is one of the great Old Testament prophets, taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire.

clue.text: Like my poor neighbour at the card table

definitions.text: Like my poor neighbour at the card table

parts.words: Like my poor neighbour at the card table
parts.note: the card game called beggar-my-neighbour, in which the aim is to win all the other player's cards

explanation.surface: Sympathy for the impoverished person sitting beside me at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Beggar-my-neighbour is a children's card game; the neighbour who loses everything has been made poor by it.
explanation.definitionFit: In beggar-my-neighbour the losing neighbour is stripped of every card, reduced to poverty.

clue.text: Metaphorically the key of the door, of course

definitions.text: Metaphorically the key of the door
definitions.meaning: the right of admission or access to a place or society
a dish served as one course of a meal

explanation.definitionFit: The French word means admission, a figurative key, and also a dish forming one stage of a meal.

clue.text: Pertaining to the more mysterious coteries

definitions.text: Pertaining to the more mysterious coteries

indicators.note: mysterious suggests the clique's letters are arranged in a puzzling new order

explanation.surface: A description of the more secretive inner circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meant only for a small circle of initiates is obscure and private to such groups.
